edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts point in more than one direction, so no single pooled effect estimate is reliable enough to summarize cleanly.
edges.mechanism: The interaction hypothesis is that genotype changes how the exposure is handled or translated into downstream biology, whether through lipoprotein trafficking, one-carbon metabolism, appetite regulation, or lactose-related dietary behavior. For Cardiovascular disease, that means any observed effect should be read as effect modification, not genetic destiny.
edges.summary: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts link lactase persistence with high dairy intake to mixed effects on cardiovascular disease in adults with lactase persistence. The average effect is usually unknown rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
